title: Let AI Draft Routine Replies, Keep the Human on the Conversation
subtitle: Use suggestions to reduce repetitive wording without delegating the relationship
description: For repetitive support or service messages, AI can propose a response from the case facts and approved guidance while the human checks diagnosis, policy, tone, and the actual next step. Large-scale field evidence supports gains in one customer-support setting, especially for less experienced workers.

lifeOsSource.hack: Use AI to propose a routine customer reply from verified case facts, then let the human correct the diagnosis, policy, tone, and next action.
lifeOsSource.whatYouDo: Provide only information you are allowed to share, plus the customer question and approved policy or knowledge source. Ask for a concise draft. Check that it answers the real issue, does not invent policy or status, and gives the correct next action before sending.
lifeOsSource.checkIn: Did the suggestion save wording effort while leaving the human more attentive to the customer's actual problem?
lifeOsSource.reference: Brynjolfsson, Li & Raymond (2025) — Generative AI at Work

faq.question: Does this mean AI should answer customers autonomously?
faq.answer: No. The cited field study examined an assistant that suggested responses to human agents. The agents remained responsible for the conversation and could edit or ignore suggestions.

faq.question: What should always be checked?
faq.answer: Case facts, account or order status, policy, promised actions, deadlines, pricing, safety-sensitive information, and anything that could create a commitment or escalation.

intro.html: A support reply has two jobs: communicate clearly and move the real case forward. AI can help with the first. It only helps with the second when the underlying facts and policy are right.

sections.title: 1. Ground the draft
sections.html: Give the model the verified case facts and the policy or knowledge material it is allowed to use. Avoid asking it to infer account state or policy from thin context.

sections.title: 2. Draft the response
sections.html: Ask for a concise answer that states what is known, what happens next, and any action required from the customer. Keep routine wording routine.

sections.title: 3. Check the diagnosis before the prose
sections.html: A beautiful response to the wrong problem is still the wrong response. Confirm that the draft addresses the actual issue and that any troubleshooting step is appropriate.

sections.title: 4. Edit as the accountable human
sections.html: Adjust tone, remove invented certainty, and verify commitments before sending. Escalate cases that exceed the known policy or evidence.

references.title: Generative AI at Work
references.claim_scope: A staggered deployment study involving 5,172 customer-support agents found AI assistance increased issues resolved per hour by 15% on average, with larger gains for less experienced and lower-skilled agents. The setting used a specific firm, workflow, and assistant and does not imply identical gains elsewhere.

editorialCuration.reason: Translate strong workplace evidence into a bounded human-in-the-loop reply workflow without extending the causal claim beyond the studied customer-support setting.
